questions.question: The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants was adopted at a Conference of Plenipotentiaries in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)** was adopted in **2001** at a Conference of Plenipotentiaries held in Stockholm, Sweden.
 
• This **Convention** is a global treaty aimed at protecting human health and the environment from chemicals that persist in the environment, accumulate in living organisms, and pose risks to human health.
 
• It specifically targets chemicals that are toxic, resistant to environmental degradation, and can be transported across international boundaries. *Hence, the adoption year is correctly stated as 2001.*
 
• **Major objectives:** The Convention seeks to eliminate or restrict the production and use of persistent organic pollutants (POPs). It also aims at reducing releases of these pollutants into the environment.
 
• The Convention initially addressed 12 specific chemicals known as the "dirty dozen," including pesticides like DDT and industrial chemicals like PCBs. Over time, more chemicals have been added to the list. *Hence, the Convention's focus is highly significant.*
 
• **Implementation:** The Convention requires parties to develop national implementation plans and take measures to reduce or eliminate the release of POPs. It also promotes international cooperation and support for capacity building in developing countries.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 2001.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs):**

 
 
• **POPs** are chemical substances that persist in the environment, bioaccumulate through the food chain, and pose a risk to human health and ecosystems.
 
• They include **pesticides, industrial chemicals, and unintentional by-products** like dioxins and furans.
 
 
 
• **History of the Stockholm Convention:**
 
 
• The Convention was adopted in **2001** and came into force on **May 17, 2004**, following ratification by the required number of countries.
 
• It was initiated by the United Nations Environment Programme (**UNEP**) to address global concerns regarding toxic chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Convention:**
 
 
• It has contributed significantly to global environmental protection by reducing the production and use of harmful chemicals.
 
• The Convention also promotes sustainable practices and the use of safer alternatives.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of the Stockholm Convention:**

 
 
• The Convention targets **POPs** under three categories: **intentionally produced chemicals** (like pesticides and industrial chemicals), **unintentionally produced chemicals** (like dioxins), and those slated for elimination or restriction.
 
• It promotes the use of **best environmental practices (BEPs)** and **best available techniques (BATs)** to minimize releases of POPs.
 
 
 
• **Examples of POPs:**
 
 
• **DDT:** A pesticide banned in many countries due to its harmful effects on health and the environment.
 
• **PCBs:** Industrial chemicals used in electrical equipment, now restricted globally.
 
• **Dioxins:** Unintentionally produced during industrial processes; highly toxic.

__

This feature is particularly useful for users who prefer keyboard shortcuts or have accessibility needs.
 
• When the **Alt** key is pressed, Windows highlights the menu bar and displays the underlined letters for each menu option. The user can then press the corresponding letter to open the desired menu.
 
• This method is widely used in applications like **Microsoft Word, Excel, and other Windows-based software**, where menus such as File, Edit, View, etc., can be navigated using this shortcut.
 
• This functionality is part of the Windows design to enhance **accessibility** and improve user interaction, making it faster and more efficient for users to access menu options without a mouse. *Hence, the correct answer is pressing Alt and the underlined letter in the menu title.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2:** Right-clicking on the **title bar** does not access the menu bar; it usually opens a context menu for window controls such as minimize, maximize, or close. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Option 4:** Pressing **F5** typically refreshes the current page or window but does not open the menu bar. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Importance of keyboard shortcuts:** Keyboard shortcuts like Alt + underlined letter help users save time and enhance productivity. They are an integral part of the **Windows operating system's user interface**, especially for professionals who use Windows applications extensively.
 
• **Applications:** This functionality is available across several **Windows-based programs**, making it consistent and easy for users to remember and apply across different software.

questions.question: When was the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) launched by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __** Apr 12 2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)** was launched by the **Government of India** on **April 12, 2005**. It aimed to provide accessible, affordable, and quality healthcare to the rural population, especially vulnerable groups.
 
• The mission was introduced as part of the **National Health Policy** to address deficiencies in healthcare infrastructure and improve health indicators like **infant mortality rate** and **maternal mortality rate**.
 
• NRHM primarily targeted **18 states** where health indicators were particularly poor. These included states like **Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh**, and others.
 
• The mission focused on strengthening the public health system through interventions like **ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)**, improving infrastructure, and integrating primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare services.
 
• NRHM also worked on improving **sanitation, nutrition, and safe drinking water** as complementary health interventions. It sought to reduce gaps in healthcare access between urban and rural areas.
 
• The mission emphasized **community participation** and introduced mechanisms for decentralization to empower local health facilities and improve their functionality.
 
• The **Janani Suraksha Yojana**, a key component of NRHM, aimed to promote institutional deliveries and reduce maternal and infant mortality rates.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Tue Apr 12 2005.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of NRHM:**

 
 
• **Strengthening rural healthcare infrastructure:** Building new health facilities like **Primary Health Centres (PHCs)**, **Community Health Centres (CHCs)**, and sub-centres.
 
• **Human resources:** Recruiting healthcare workers, including **ASHA workers**, nurses, and doctors, to fill gaps in rural health services.
 
• **Disease control:** Strengthening programs for communicable diseases like **malaria, tuberculosis, and HIV/AIDS**, as well as non-communicable diseases.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• **ASHA workers:** Serving as a bridge between the healthcare system and the community, these workers provided essential health services and promoted awareness.
 
• **Decentralization:** Empowering **local governing bodies** like Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to plan and implement health initiatives.
 
• **Janani Suraksha Yojana:** Financial incentives for institutional deliveries to reduce maternal and infant mortality.
 
 
 
• **Achievements:**
 
 
• **Increased institutional deliveries:** A rise in institutional deliveries was observed across states due to programs like **Janani Suraksha Yojana**.
 
• **Improved health indicators:** Significant improvements were seen in **infant mortality rate**, **maternal mortality rate**, and life expectancy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NRHM's integration:** In 2013, NRHM was subsumed under the **National Health Mission (NHM)**, which also included the **National Urban Health Mission (NUHM)**.
 
• **Focus Areas:** NRHM prioritized **maternal health, child health, family planning, communicable diseases**, and infrastructure development.
 
• **Funding Mechanism:** The mission received funding through a mix of **central and state government contributions**, ensuring shared responsibility.

questions.question: The Dutch East India Company established its first factory in India in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Petapuli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Petapuli** was the first location where the **Dutch East India Company** established its factory in India. It was set up in the early **17th century**.
 
• The Dutch East India Company, also known as the **Vereenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie (VOC)**, started operations in India primarily for the purpose of trade, especially in **spices**.
 
• Petapuli, located in **Tamil Nadu**, was chosen due to its strategic location and proximity to spice-producing areas. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• The **Dutch East India Company** was among the first European powers to establish trading posts in India, alongside the Portuguese and the British.
 
• Other locations such as **Calicut** and **Goa** were primarily associated with Portuguese influence, while **Pondicherry** was a French colony. *Hence, the other options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dutch East India Company:**

 
 
• The **Dutch East India Company** was founded in **1602** by the Dutch Republic to manage its trade in Asia.
 
• It was primarily involved in trading **spices, textiles, and other goods**. India became an important region for trading due to its **diverse resources**.
 
• The company established several factories in India, including those in **Masulipatnam, Chinsurah, and Nagapattinam**, apart from Petapuli.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Petapuli:**
 
 
• Petapuli became the first base for the Dutch in India, enabling them to establish a strong foothold in the region for trading.
 
• It was located near spice-producing areas, making it a strategic choice for trade in **pepper, cardamom, and other spices**.
 
 
 
• **Other European Powers in India:**
 
 
• The **Portuguese** were the first European power to arrive in India, with their base in **Goa**.
 
• The **British East India Company** arrived later, establishing its first factory at **Surat** in **1612**.
 
• The **French** established their primary base in **Pondicherry**, which became a significant center for French influence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Trade Items:**

 
 
• The Dutch primarily traded in **spices**, including **pepper, cinnamon, cloves**, and **nutmeg**, which were highly valuable in Europe.
 
• They also traded in **textiles** and **indigo**, which were produced in various parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Dutch Influence:**
 
 
• The Dutch influence in India started declining after the rise of the **British East India Company**, which became the dominant European power.
 
• By the **18th century**, Dutch operations were limited to a few trading posts.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Dutch left behind an influence on Indian architecture, cuisine, and culture, especially in regions where they were established.
 
• Their trading practices also contributed to the development of trade systems in India during the colonial era.

questions.question: Why is an alloy considered a mixture even though it cannot be separated by physical methods?

options.text: It is formed only by non-metals.
It shows the properties of its constituents and can have variable composition.
It contains only one type of element in vapor form.
Alloys are always magnetic because they contain metals with a fixed composition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It shows the properties of its constituents and can have variable composition.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An alloy is considered a mixture:** Alloys are physical combinations of metals or metals and non-metals. They are not chemically bonded, which is why they are classified as mixtures.
 
• They show the **properties of their constituent elements**. For example, steel combines the strength of iron with the corrosion resistance of carbon.
 
• An alloy can have a **variable composition**, meaning the proportion of different elements can change. For instance, brass can contain variable amounts of copper and zinc, depending on the desired properties. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Alloys cannot be separated by **simple physical methods**, such as filtration, because their components are mixed at the atomic level. However, they can still be separated chemically, reinforcing the idea that they are mixtures and not compounds.
 
• The **appearance, strength, and conductivity** of an alloy depend on the elements used and their proportions. Examples include brass, bronze, and stainless steel. *Hence, the correct answer is the given option.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Alloys:**

 
 
• **Alloys** are a combination of two or more elements, where at least one is a metal.
 
• Alloys are created to enhance the **properties of metals**, such as durability, strength, and corrosion resistance.
 
• **Example:** Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, used for decorative purposes and in tools.
 
• **Steel:** An alloy of iron and carbon, widely used in construction due to its strength and flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Difference between Mixtures and Compounds:**
 
 
• Mixtures are physical combinations of substances, where the individual components retain their properties.
 
• Compounds are chemically bonded substances that lose the individual properties of their components and have a fixed composition.
 
• **Alloys** fall under mixtures because their components are not chemically bonded and can have variable compositions.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Alloys:**
 
 
• **Brass:** Used in musical instruments and decorative items.
 
• **Stainless Steel:** Used in kitchenware, industrial equipment, and medical tools due to its resistance to corrosion.
 
• **Aluminum Alloys:** Lightweight and strong, used in aerospace and automobile industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Alloys:**

 
 
• Alloys are created to improve the **mechanical and chemical properties** of metals.
 
• They are widely used across industries, including **construction, transportation, electronics, and healthcare**.
 
 
 
• **Understanding Mixtures:**
 
 
• Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous. **Alloys** are homogeneous mixtures because their components are evenly distributed.
 
• **Alloys** retain the properties of their constituents, unlike compounds, which have new properties.

questions.question: In most software applications, what does Ctrl + S do if pressed multiple times?

options.text: Updates the saved file without creating a new one
Saves a new copy each time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Updates the saved file without creating a new one**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In most software applications, pressing **Ctrl + S** performs the function of saving the current document or file. It is commonly used across text editors, spreadsheets, graphic design tools, and other software.
 
• When **Ctrl + S** is pressed multiple times, the existing file is updated each time. It does **not create a new file**, but rather overwrites the previous saved version of the file with the current changes.
 
• The functionality ensures that the latest modifications are stored securely without affecting the original file's name or its location. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• Option 2 ("Reverts the document") is incorrect because pressing **Ctrl + S** only saves changes and does not revert the document to a previous state.
 
• Option 3 ("Saves a new copy each time") is incorrect since using **Ctrl + S** does not create duplicate copies. Instead, it modifies and updates the existing file.
 
• Option 4 ("Deletes the previous version") is incorrect as saving does not delete the previous version. It simply updates the file with the latest changes.
 
• Option 5 is incomplete and does not provide a valid functionality for **Ctrl + S**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Updates the saved file without creating a new one.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Usage of Ctrl + S:**

 
 
• **Ctrl + S** is a universal keyboard shortcut used to save files in various software applications such as **Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint**, graphic editing software like **Photoshop**, and even coding environments like **Visual Studio Code**.
 
• This shortcut is essential for **data preservation** and avoids losing progress due to unexpected software or system crashes.
 
 
 
• **File Saving Behavior:**
 
 
• When saving a file using **Ctrl + S**, the software updates the current file's contents without altering its name or location.
 
• If saving for the first time, most applications prompt users to specify a location and a name for the file. Subsequent saves will overwrite the file at the specified location.
 
• **Example:** If you save a Word document named "Report.docx" using **Ctrl + S**, the changes will be saved to "Report.docx" without creating a new file.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Frequent Saving:**
 
 
• Regularly using **Ctrl + S** minimizes the risk of data loss due to unexpected events like software crashes or power outages.
 
• Some software applications even include an **auto-save feature**, ensuring periodic saving without manual intervention.
 
• For example, in **Google Docs**, changes are saved automatically as you type, eliminating the need for manual saving.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Saving:**

 
 
• Saving ensures **data integrity**, allowing users to preserve their progress and access updated files later.
 
• Some applications also allow saving under a new name or location using the **"Save As"** option, which creates a new file while retaining the original document.
 
 
 
• **Software-Specific Functionalities:**
 
 
• **Microsoft Word:** Ctrl + S updates the document and retains its formatting and layout.
 
• **Adobe Photoshop:** Ctrl + S saves the current project in its original format, while Ctrl + Shift + S enables saving in a different format or location.
 
• **Visual Studio Code:** Ctrl + S is used to save code files, ensuring real-time updates for testing and debugging.

questions.question: Which department, headed by Dabir-i-Khas, handled royal correspondence and official communication during the Delhi Sultanate?

It was headed by an official called the **Dabir-i-Khas**, who ensured the accuracy and confidentiality of the Sultan’s communications.
 
• The Dabir-i-Khas was tasked with drafting letters, preparing official decrees, and maintaining records of state correspondence. **Hence, statement is correct.**
 
• The department’s role was critical in ensuring smooth administration, as communication between various provinces, officials, and the Sultan was facilitated through it.
 
• It played an essential part in maintaining the Sultanate’s centralized administrative structure, which relied heavily on written orders and decrees.
 
• **Diwan-i-Insha** was instrumental in safeguarding official secrets and preventing unauthorized access to sensitive information. This ensured the Sultan’s commands were followed without compromise. **Hence, the statement is correct.**
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Diwan-i-Insha.***

• **Barid-i-Mumalik:** This department was in charge of **intelligence and espionage**. It gathered information about internal and external threats to the Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate Administration:**
 
 
• The administration was highly centralized, with the Sultan as the supreme authority. Departments like **Diwan-i-Insha** played a vital role in executing and communicating royal orders.
 
• The Sultanate maintained a structured bureaucracy, with each department headed by skilled officials to ensure efficient governance.
 
 
 
• **Important Functions of Diwan-i-Insha:**

• Ensuring confidentiality and security of state communications.
 
• Maintaining records of important correspondence and written orders.

• The Bose-Einstein condensate was formed using the isotope **Rubidium-87**. This isotope was chosen for its suitable atomic properties that allowed cooling down to extremely low temperatures.
 
• **Bose-Einstein condensates** occur when a group of bosonic atoms is cooled to temperatures close to absolute zero, where they occupy the lowest quantum state and behave like a single entity.

• This achievement proved the theoretical predictions made by **Satyendra Nath Bose** and **Albert Einstein** decades earlier regarding the behavior of bosonic particles at near-zero temperatures.
 
• The creation of the Bose-Einstein condensate marked a major milestone in quantum mechanics and opened new avenues for research in fields such as **quantum computing** and **precision measurement.**

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution states, 'no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law'?

__
 
• **Article 300A** of the **Constitution of India** states that **'no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.'**
 
• This article was added to the Constitution of India by the **44th Amendment Act** in **1978**, replacing the original provision in **Article 31**, which guaranteed the right to property as a fundamental right.
 
• The right to property under **Article 300A** is now a **legal right** and not a **fundamental right**. Hence, it does not enjoy the same level of protection as fundamental rights under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• It ensures that the government can acquire private property only through legal procedures and by providing compensation as per the laws governing land acquisition. This protects individuals from arbitrary deprivation of property.
 
• Since the statement in the question refers specifically to the provision about deprivation of property by authority of law, **Article 300A** correctly addresses this issue. *Hence, the correct answer is Article 300A.*

__
 
• **Article 300A of the Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 300A** is part of **Part XII** of the Constitution, dealing with property, contracts, liabilities, obligations, and suits.
 
• It ensures that property cannot be taken away from an individual unless authorized by a **legislative provision**.
 
• It empowers the government to acquire property for public purposes, provided there is a legal basis and adequate compensation.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Before **1978**, the **right to property** was a fundamental right under **Article 31**. However, due to issues with land reforms and equitable distribution of resources, it was removed from Part III and made a legal right under **Article 300A**.
 
• **44th Amendment Act:** Passed in **1978**, this amendment transformed the right to property into a constitutional but non-fundamental right.
 
• The change was intended to prioritize socio-economic justice over individual property rights.
 
 
 
• **Legal Implications:**
 
 
• As a legal right, violations of **Article 300A** can be challenged in a court of law, but it does not fall under the ambit of the **fundamental rights**, which can be directly enforced under **Article 32**.
 
• The government is obligated to follow due process and provide compensation when acquiring property.

• As a legal right, **Article 300A** does not offer the same level of constitutional protection as fundamental rights like **Article 14** (Right to Equality) or **Article 19** (Freedom of Speech).
 
• However, it still provides a safeguard against arbitrary actions by the state concerning property ownership.
 
 
 
• **Land Acquisition Laws:**

questions.question: What key emotion did the Extremists aim to arouse in people against British colonial rule?

• **Techniques:** Extremists used powerful rhetoric, boycott movements, Swadeshi campaigns, and public demonstrations to channel indignation into collective action. These methods were highly effective in awakening political consciousness among the masses.
 
• Unlike Moderates, who believed in negotiations and petitions, Extremists advocated for direct action and self-reliance, appealing to the emotions of anger and pride among Indians to fight against colonial oppression.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Indignation.***

• **Key Movements and Leaders:**

• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** Known as the "Father of Indian Unrest," Tilak used newspapers like **Kesari** and **Maratha** to highlight British injustices and arouse indignation.

questions.question: In which of the following years were the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms introduced by the British Government in India to gradually establish self-governing institutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms** were introduced in **1919** to provide limited self-governance to Indians. The reforms were named after the then Secretary of State for India, Edwin Montagu, and the Viceroy, Lord Chelmsford.
 
• The reforms were associated with the **Government of India Act, 1919**, which aimed to increase Indian participation in governance.
 
• The system of **diarchy** was introduced at the provincial level, dividing powers between elected Indian ministers and British officials. Certain subjects were reserved for British officials, while others were transferred to Indian ministers.
 
• The reforms provided for a bicameral legislature at the central level and expanded the electorate by introducing limited franchise based on property, education, and income qualifications.
 
• The reforms were criticized for being inadequate in meeting the demands for full self-governance and were seen as a tool to placate growing demands for independence.
 
• The **Montagu Declaration** of 1917 laid the foundation for these reforms, promising gradual development of Indian self-governing institutions.
 
• These reforms led to dissatisfaction among Indians, which ultimately contributed to the rise of the **Non-Cooperation Movement** led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 1919.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919:**

 
 
• This act marked the beginning of constitutional reforms in British India.
 
• Introduced a **dual government system** or diarchy at the provincial level. Reserved subjects like police, justice, and irrigation were controlled by British officials, while transferred subjects like education, health, and agriculture were handled by Indian ministers.
 
 
 
• **Montagu Declaration of 1917:**
 
 
• This declaration was a promise of **self-governance** for Indians in the future, which led to the formulation of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
 
• It was meant to address the growing political unrest and demands for independence in India.
 
 
 
• **Criticisms of the Reforms:**
 
 
• The diarchy system was criticized for limiting real power for Indians, as the reserved subjects remained under British control.
 
• The franchise was very limited and excluded a majority of the Indian population.
 
• The reforms failed to address the demands for complete self-rule and were thus seen as a failed attempt to pacify Indians.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical context:**

 
 
• The reforms were introduced after World War I, during a time of increasing political awareness and activism among Indians.
 
• The **Home Rule Movement**, led by leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant, played a significant role in pressuring the British government for reforms.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Reforms:**
 
 
• The limited reforms led to widespread dissatisfaction and the initiation of the **Non-Cooperation Movement** under Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• These reforms laid the groundwork for subsequent acts like the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which further expanded self-governance but still fell short of granting independence.
 
• They are a significant milestone in India's constitutional development, showcasing the early stages of India's struggle for self-rule.

questions.question: Which drainage pattern resembles the branches of a tree and is common in rivers of the northern plains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dendritic drainage pattern.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dendritic drainage pattern:** This type of drainage pattern resembles the branches of a tree, with tributaries joining the main river at acute angles. It is the most common drainage pattern found in nature.
 
• This pattern develops where the river flows over homogeneous rock types that offer uniform resistance to erosion, allowing water to spread out naturally. *Hence, this drainage pattern resembles the northern plains.*
 
• It is often seen in regions with a flat or slightly undulating terrain, such as the **northern plains of India**, where rivers like the **Ganga, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra** flow. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• **Other drainage patterns:** Trellis, Centripetal, and Radial drainage patterns differ significantly from the dendritic pattern and are formed under different geological conditions. These are not common in the rivers of the northern plains. *Hence, they are incorrect options.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Trellis drainage pattern:**

 
 
• This pattern is characterized by tributaries flowing parallel to each other and joining the main river at right angles. It forms in regions with alternating layers of hard and soft rock, such as in the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal drainage pattern:**
 
 
• Here, rivers converge towards a central depression or basin. This pattern is found in areas like the **Rann of Kutch** in India.
 
 
 
• **Radial drainage pattern:**
 
 
• In this pattern, rivers radiate outward from a central point, often a hill or volcanic cone. An example is the **rivers flowing outward from the Amarkantak Plateau.**
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of drainage patterns:**
 
 
• Drainage patterns reflect the geological structure and topography of a region. The type of rock, slope, and climatic factors determine the formation of these patterns.
 
• **Examples:** Dendritic drainage is common in the plains, trellis in folded terrains, centripetal in basins, and radial around elevated points.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Formation of drainage patterns:**

 
 
• Drainage patterns form due to the interaction of geological processes such as erosion, deposition, and tectonic activity.
 
• The terrain's slope, rock type, and climate play a crucial role in shaping the drainage system.
 
 
 
• **Impact on human activities:**
 
 
• Drainage patterns influence agriculture, settlement, and the construction of infrastructure like dams and canals.
 
• For instance, the **Ganga river basin** supports dense human settlement due to its fertile soil and efficient drainage system.

• The agreement formally introduced the concept of **inflation targeting** to India's monetary policy, with the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** as the benchmark.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Reserve Bank of India under MPFA:**

• **Impact of MPFA:**
 
 
• The agreement improved **coordination** between the government and RBI, leading to better policy alignment.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a key function of Subordinate Courts in India?

• The structure of Subordinate Courts includes **District Courts, Sessions Courts, Magistrates Courts, and Civil Courts**. These courts have specific jurisdiction based on the nature of the case.

• Subordinate Courts do not interpret **international treaties**. This function is reserved for higher courts like the Supreme Court. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Subordinate Courts do not have the authority to **review decisions of High Courts**. This power is exclusively vested in the Supreme Court. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

questions.question: What is the correct order of arrival of seismic waves at a seismograph after an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P-waves, S-waves, surface waves.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seismic waves are generated during an earthquake** and are detected by a seismograph. These waves travel through the Earth's interior and surface.
 
• **P-waves (Primary waves):** These are the first waves to arrive at the seismograph because they travel the fastest. They are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles move in the same direction as the wave propagation. P-waves can travel through solids, liquids, and gases.
 
• **S-waves (Secondary waves):** These waves arrive after the P-waves because they travel slower. S-waves are transverse waves, meaning the particles move perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. They can only travel through solids. *Hence, the order places S-waves after P-waves.*
 
• **Surface waves:** These are the slowest seismic waves and arrive last at the seismograph. They travel along the Earth's surface and cause most of the damage during an earthquake due to their high amplitude. They include Love waves and Rayleigh waves. *Hence, surface waves are detected after P-waves and S-waves.*
 
• The sequence of arrival is determined by the speed of propagation of each wave. *Hence, the correct order is P-waves, S-waves, and surface waves.*
 
• ***Thus, the correct answer is P-waves, S-waves, surface waves.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Seismic waves classification:**

 
 
• **Body waves:** These travel through the Earth's interior and include P-waves and S-waves. P-waves are faster and can travel through all states of matter, while S-waves are slower and can only travel through solids.
 
• **Surface waves:** These travel along the Earth's surface and include Love waves and Rayleigh waves. They cause significant damage during earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of seismic waves:**
 
 
• **P-waves:** Longitudinal waves with the fastest speed. They are the least destructive due to their low amplitude.
 
• **S-waves:** Transverse waves with slower speed than P-waves. They cause more damage than P-waves due to higher amplitude.
 
• **Surface waves:** These are the slowest and most destructive waves due to their high amplitude and energy concentrated near the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Uses of seismic wave analysis:**
 
 
• Helps in determining the epicenter and magnitude of earthquakes.
 
• Provides insights into Earth's interior structure, such as the crust, mantle, and core.
 
• Used in geophysical studies and exploration for resources like oil and gas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seismograph:** A device used to measure and record seismic waves. It provides data on the arrival time and amplitude of waves.
 
• **Earthquake magnitude:** A measure of the energy released during an earthquake, commonly measured using the Richter scale.
 
• **Epicenter:** The point on the Earth's surface directly above the earthquake's focus. It is determined using the difference in arrival times of P-waves and S-waves.
 
• **Seismic wave propagation:** The speed depends on the medium's density and elasticity. For example, P-waves travel faster in denser and elastic media.

questions.question: Which of the following Buddhist texts is often called the 'Gita of Buddhism' for its importance and teachings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhammapada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dhammapada** is one of the most revered texts in Buddhism, often referred to as the "Gita of Buddhism" due to its significance in spreading the teachings of Lord Buddha.
 
• It is a collection of 423 verses, divided into 26 chapters, and presents the core principles of Buddhist philosophy in a simple and poetic form.
 
• The name "Dhammapada" translates to "Words of the Dharma," and it is considered a guide to moral conduct, spiritual awakening, and self-discipline.
 
• The verses of the **Dhammapada** emphasize themes like the impermanence of life, the importance of mindfulness, and the path to enlightenment. *Hence, the correct option is Dhammapada.*
 
• It is part of the Khuddaka Nikaya, a division of the Sutta Pitaka, which is one of the three baskets of the Buddhist canon, the Tripitaka.
 
• The **Dhammapada** has been translated into multiple languages and is studied worldwide for its spiritual depth and practical wisdom.
 
• Unlike other Buddhist texts that may focus on narrative or abstract teachings, the **Dhammapada** provides concise, actionable wisdom applicable to daily life. *Hence, it is rightly called the "Gita of Buddhism."*
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Dhammapada.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Dhammapada:**

 
 
• The **Dhammapada** is believed to have been compiled around the 3rd century BCE and is attributed to the teachings of Lord Buddha.
 
• It serves as a practical guide for individuals seeking to follow the Middle Path, emphasizing virtues like non-violence, self-restraint, and compassion.
 
• Its verses are often quoted in Buddhist literature and are used for moral instruction and spiritual reflection.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Mahayana Sutra:** This refers to texts associated with Mahayana Buddhism, which emphasize the Bodhisattva path. However, they are not considered equivalent to the "Gita of Buddhism."
 
• **Vamsathapakasini:** This is a commentary on the Mahavamsa and is primarily a historical text, not focused on spiritual teachings.
 
• **Saddharmapundarīka Sūtra:** Known as the Lotus Sutra, it is an important Mahayana text, but its thematic scope differs from the Dhammapada.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Dhammapada:**
 
 
• The **Dhammapada** is widely regarded as one of the most accessible and practical Buddhist scriptures for beginners and scholars alike.
 
• It has inspired numerous philosophical works and continues to be a central text for those studying Buddhism worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Themes of the Dhammapada:**

 
 
• It emphasizes the importance of **mindfulness**, stating that the mind is the source of all actions and should be trained wisely.
 
• It promotes **compassion** and encourages individuals to live harmoniously with others.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **Dhammapada** reflects the foundational principles laid down by Lord Buddha, making it an essential text for understanding early Buddhist philosophy.
 
• Its poetic nature makes it easy to remember and recite, which contributed to its widespread popularity.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right protects citizens from being forced into labour or human trafficking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right against Exploitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right against Exploitation** is one of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It is defined under **Articles 23 and 24** of the Constitution, which aim to protect citizens from exploitation.
 
• **Article 23** prohibits **human trafficking, begar (forced labor), and similar forms of forced labor**. It declares such practices as illegal and punishable under the law. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Article 24** prohibits the employment of children below the age of **14 years** in factories, mines, or other hazardous occupations. This provision ensures protection for children from exploitation in unsafe work environments. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The **Right against Exploitation** is critical in safeguarding the dignity of individuals and preventing exploitative practices that violate basic human rights.
 
• This right ensures that every individual has the freedom to live without being subjected to forced labor or any form of exploitation. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Right against Exploitation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 23:**

 
 
• **Article 23** explicitly prohibits practices like **human trafficking**, bonded labor, and begar. These acts are considered crimes against human dignity.
 
• It applies to both **citizens** and **non-citizens** within the territory of India, making it a universal right.
 
• The government has introduced laws such as the **Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956** to enforce Article 23 and curb human trafficking effectively.
 
 
 
• **Article 24:**
 
 
• **Article 24** prohibits the employment of children below the age of **14 years** in hazardous industries and occupations.
 
• This provision is complemented by laws like the **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**, which provides guidelines to prevent child labor.
 
• It aims to ensure that children are not deprived of their right to education and are protected from exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Role of Judiciary:**
 
 
• The judiciary has played a significant role in upholding the **Right against Exploitation** through landmark judgments and interpretations.
 
• For example, in the case of **People's Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India (1982)**, the Supreme Court declared that any form of forced labor is unconstitutional under Article 23.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• **Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956:** This law criminalizes human trafficking and related exploitative practices, enforcing Article 23.
 
• **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986:** This legislation prohibits employment of children under hazardous conditions, enforcing Article 24.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights serve as the cornerstone of India's democracy, ensuring equality and justice for all citizens.
 
• The **Right against Exploitation** plays a critical role in safeguarding human dignity and eliminating exploitative practices from society.
